edges.description: Sustained kinase signalling drives the proliferation that forms the tumour
The polysomies are acquired after the initiating lesion rather than alongside it.
The proliferating spindle-cell population is the renal mass that presents.
A growing fetal renal mass is the first thing the pregnancy shows, through excess amniotic fluid.
A minority of these tumours secrete parathyroid hormone-related protein.
A renal mass raises blood pressure, and the hypertension resolves once it is removed.
The mass bleeds into the collecting system.
In the cellular subtype the tumour can metastasise to bone, where it destroys it.
Circulating PTHrP mobilises calcium from bone.

nodes.description: The duplicated EGFR kinase domain, and the fusion-bound NTRK3 kinase domain, signal without ligand. This is the point at which the three lesion classes converge on one mechanism, which is why the entry models them as separate upstream lesions feeding a shared node.

nodes.description: A selective TRK inhibitor, used in the fusion-positive cellular subtype where the tumour is not resectable or has metastasised. The cached evidence runs both ways: a dramatic bone remodelling response in one ETV6::NTRK3 case, and in a TPM3::NTRK1 case a response at metastatic sites followed by acquired resistance and death.

nodes.description: The initiating event is an acquired kinase lesion in a renal or perirenal mesenchymal progenitor, arising in utero. Three lesion classes are established, and they segregate by subtype rather than co-occurring: the EGFR kinase-domain internal tandem duplication, the ETV6::NTRK3 fusion, and rarer intragenic BRAF rearrangement.
